sentence: This project studies how two calcium signaling pathways in vascular smooth muscle cells affect blood pressure, both normally and in hypertension.
This project studies how a repeated stretch of DNA expands in an inherited ataxia and how that leads to disease.
This project builds a platform with stem cell models of the neuromuscular junction to measure the potency of Botulinum toxin without mouse tests.
This project tries to find out what controls how insulin and glucagon are released over time, using microfluidic devices.
This project studies single-cell gene activity and chromatin accessibility in youth with type 2 diabetes compared to healthy youth.
This project studies how problems with DNA methylation, a process that controls gene activity, lead to colon cancer.
This project builds sensors that track cells in real time while they are grown, and tries to control how those cells behave.
This project tries to find out how the liver gene tribbles pseudokinase 1 controls protein degradation and how that relates to cardiometabolic disease.
This project studies how environmental stress affects the risk of Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias in people living in cities and rural areas.
This project uses wearable data to study how the built environment affects physical activity and health outcomes.
This project studies how mRNA vaccine particles work against glioblastoma, including how they assemble, move in cells and trigger a T cell response.
This project uses rats exposed to a mixture of endocrine-disrupting chemicals to find out how they cause behavioral and metabolic problems.
This project studies how proteins and biochemical pathways drive cell division, and why cells end up with the wrong number of chromosomes.
This project builds statistical and machine learning methods to model gene expression, DNA-protein binding and three-dimensional DNA structure in single cells.
This project builds a biobank of postmortem samples from free-ranging rhesus macaques and measures them to study aging.
This project develops a small molecule that blocks an epigenic pathway to grow back alveolar bone lost to periodontitis.
This project studies how genes are regulated, from chromatin and transcription to RNA biology, to understand changes in cancer.
This project tries to find enzyme inhibitors that block colibactin, a metabolite made by gut bacteria and linked to colorectal cancer.
This project uses gene editing to cut HIV DNA out of host cells and boost immune cells, aiming to cure HIV.
This project provides CRISPR tools and viral vectors that let researchers edit genes in cells and animals.
